item.text:
**3B.6 Research Note**

Bottom line: I found no strong evidence that Hasina reduced domestic fear and insecurity in 2024 without replacing it with state terror or a broader political fear climate. The record is dominated by curfews, internet shutdowns, military deployment, and blame-shifting during the student protests. The only weak counterevidence is a defensive Rohingya/border posture that addresses external security, not domestic fear.

- [Bangladesh blocks roads and internet, deploys army to curb protests](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-blocks-roads-and-internet-deploys-army-to-curb-protests/2183179/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024. Claim: Soldiers patrolled Dhaka, roadblocks went up, and internet/text services were suspended during the protest crackdown; this is strong evidence of fear-producing coercive control rather than fear reduction. IDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`
- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024. Claim: Hasina blamed political opponents for the violence and kept the curfew in place, which reads as political fear management through scapegoating and coercion rather than restoring public security. IDs: `3B.6`, `3B.3`, `3B.5`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`
- [Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448) — Reuters, July 26, 2024. Claim: Reuters said the government imposed a comprehensive internet outage and countrywide curfew, a tactic it had used previously at refugee camps and ahead of elections; that supports a broader climate of intimidation and information control. IDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.1`
- [Bangladesh restores internet as students call off job-quota protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-restores-internet-as-students-call-off-jobquota-protests-3540555) — Reuters, July 29, 2024. Claim: Internet service was restored only after protests were called off and conditions were said to be returning to normal; this is the closest weak counterevidence, but it reflects de-escalation after coercive disruption, not a proactive fear-reduction strategy. IDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`
- [Exclusive-Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina's fate](https://www.voanews.com/a/exclusive-bangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasina-s-fate/7733166.html) — Reuters, August 7, 2024. Claim: The army refused to open fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew, implying the coercive apparatus had been pushed toward lethal domestic enforcement; that is incompatible with a low-fear, rights-respecting security posture. IDs: `3B.6`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh will not let in any more Rohingya refugees - minister](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-will-not-let-in-any-more-rohingya-refugees-minister/1958020/) — Reuters, February 7, 2024. Claim: Bangladesh framed refusal to admit additional Rohingya as a security necessity; this is the strongest limited positive item, but it is indirect, voiced by a minister, and concerns border management rather than reducing domestic fear. IDs: `3B.6`, `2B.3`
- [Bangladesh ramps up border vigilance as thousands of Rohingya flee Myanmar](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-ramps-up-border-vigilance-as-thousands-of-rohingya-flee-myanmar/2262488/) — Reuters, September 11, 2024. Claim: Bangladesh tightened border vigilance amid violence in Myanmar and refugee flows; this is a defensive security move, but it does not show reduction of domestic fear or avoidance of a broader political fear climate. IDs: `3B.6`, `2B.3`
- [Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Claim: Freedom House reports partial restrictions on internet and communications during protests, elections, and tense moments, including the July 2024 shutdown; this directly supports the conclusion that the government used control tools that amplified fear and constrained information. IDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.1`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Hasina consciously reduced domestic fear while avoiding state terror or a wider political fear climate.
- I also did not find reliable evidence of a sustained, non-coercive public-safety strategy that materially lowered fear among opponents, journalists, or protesters.
- The closest positive material is defensive border/Rohingya management, which is not strong evidence for this lens.
